question: Baking soda is prepared using which of the following processes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Solvay process**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baking soda (Sodium bicarbonate)** is primarily produced through the **Solvay process**, which is a widely used industrial chemical process.
 
• The **Solvay process** involves the reaction of **ammonia (NH₃)**, **sodium chloride (NaCl)**, and **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** in water to produce sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and other by-products.
 
• The process is energy-efficient and cost-effective, making it the preferred method for manufacturing baking soda and other related products like soda ash (sodium carbonate).
 
• Sodium bicarbonate is formed during the intermediate steps of the Solvay process when **carbon dioxide reacts with ammonia and sodium chloride in solution**, precipitating as baking soda.
 
• This process is an example of a **large-scale chemical synthesis** and has been used globally since its development by **Ernest Solvay** in the 1860s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chlor-alkali process:**

 
 
• The **Chlor-alkali process** is primarily used for producing **chlorine gas (Cl₂)**, **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, and hydrogen gas (H₂) by electrolyzing an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (brine).
 
• This process does not produce baking soda but is important for manufacturing other industrial chemicals.
 
• It is widely used in industries for applications like water treatment, paper manufacturing, and cleaning products.
 
 
 
• **Deacon’s process:**
 
 
• The **Deacon’s process** is used for manufacturing chlorine gas by oxidizing hydrogen chloride gas with atmospheric oxygen in the presence of a catalyst.
 
• This process was historically important for chlorine production but is unrelated to baking soda manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Haber process:**
 
 
• The **Haber process** is used for synthesizing **ammonia (NH₃)** from nitrogen gas (N₂) and hydrogen gas (H₂) under high pressure and temperature.
 
• This process is crucial for the fertilizer industry but does not involve baking soda production.
 
• Ammonia produced by the Haber process may be used as a raw material in the Solvay process.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Baking Soda:**
 
 
• **Baking soda** is widely used in cooking as a leavening agent to make baked goods rise.
 
• It has applications in **cleaning products**, odor control, and as a mild abrasive.
 
• Medicinally, it is used as an antacid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.
 
• In industries, baking soda is used in **fire extinguishers, textile dyeing, and leather tanning**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Solvay process details:**

 
 
• The Solvay process was developed by **Ernest Solvay**, a Belgian chemist, in **1861**.
 
• Its by-products include **calcium chloride (CaCl₂)**, which is produced during the reaction.
 
• The process operates under controlled conditions of temperature and pressure to optimize the yield of baking soda.
 
• The raw materials—**brine, limestone, and ammonia**—are inexpensive and readily available.
 
 
 
• **Global impact:**
 
 
• Baking soda produced via the Solvay process is used globally in industries ranging from food processing to pharmaceuticals.
 
• The process has minimal environmental impact compared to other chemical synthesis methods.
 
 
 
• **Historical significance:**
 
 
• The Solvay process revolutionized the chemical industry by providing a cost-effective method to manufacture sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate.
 
• It replaced older methods like the Leblanc process, which was less efficient and more polluting.
